sections.h2: What are edtech UI/UX design services?
sections.answer: Edtech UI/UX design services plan how learners move through a learning platform (UX) and design the screens they and course authors use (UI), from the learner dashboard to the mobile app.
sections.body: This work is part of our digital product design services and draws on the senior team behind our UI UX design services. As an edtech design agency, we design the learner and author screens, and your engineers build them from annotated Figma files, design tokens and component specs. The Elia Wellness dashboard pictured shows that output for a wellness learning platform.

sections.h2: Which learning screens do our edtech UI/UX design services cover?
sections.answer: Our learning platform design covers 6 parts of the product that learners and course authors use, each drawn in every screen state: default, loading, empty, error and completed.

items.title: Learner dashboard.
items.body: The next lesson, today's progress and weekly course stats show at a glance, as on the Today's Progress card we designed for Elia.

items.title: Course player.
items.body: One lesson view mixes video, text, images and challenges from the online course, with clear next and back controls, so learners keep their place in the lesson.

items.title: Course builder and admin console.
items.body: Course authors build lessons and course modules from blocks such as text, images, video and challenges, a logged-in tool our web app design services cover.

items.title: Progress tracking and badges.
items.body: Gamification, the use of game-style rewards in a learning product, should pay for finished lessons, not clicks. On Elia, lessons unlock bucket-list items such as seeing a sunrise, so learner badges mark real progress.

items.title: Learner onboarding.
items.body: Sign-up, the first lesson and a pre-course questionnaire that sets each learner's starting point, like the personal growth questionnaire Elia learners fill in on a tablet.

items.title: Mobile learning app.
items.body: Lessons and challenges on iOS and Android, with touch targets of 44×44 pt on iOS and 48×48 dp on Android, as in our mobile app UI UX design services.

sections.h2: What makes edtech UX design different from other app design?
sections.answer: Edtech UX design has to keep learners motivated over weeks on a learning platform, serve buyers who are not the users, and work for every age and ability.

items.title: Learner motivation over weeks
items.body: Learner motivation comes from finishing the course, so progress tracking and badges reward completed lessons, not taps. A streak that rewards opening the app teaches learners to open it, not to learn.

items.title: Several user groups on one platform
items.body: Learners, course authors and administrators each get their own dashboard and permissions, plus parents or teachers when children use the product. Platforms sold to institutions as software as a service (SaaS) share admin and role patterns with our SaaS UI UX design work.

items.title: Mixed ages and digital confidence
items.body: Elia's older adults had very different comfort levels with technology, so its pre-course questionnaire uses large touch targets and simple rating scales. Our usability testing services can check such patterns with your own learners.

items.title: Accessibility and privacy as buying criteria
items.body: Public schools and universities buy learning platforms against Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) accessibility rules, and products for children need parental consent before sign-up. The standards list further down names each rule and the screen it changes.

sections.h2: What did edtech UI/UX design deliver for Elia Wellness?
sections.answer: For Elia Wellness, a wellness LMS, our edtech design services took the learning platform from idea to product, and the platform reports 40% growth in user registrations.
sections.body: Elia, a wellness initiative by the Sydney Adventist Church, wanted a learning platform for older adults based on its book Live More. Scope: "idea to product, strategy, web app, mobile app and website." It centers on a social feed, a wellness score across 7 dimensions, block-based online courses, badges and progress monitoring. The platform reports a "30+ boost in wellness scores among active users." Read the Elia Wellness case study.

sections.h2: How does our edtech UI/UX design process work?
sections.answer: Our edtech UI/UX design services take a learning platform from discovery to developer handoff in 8–16 weeks (40–80 working days) and 5 steps.

items.title: Discovery and product strategy (5–10 days)
items.body: Stakeholder workshops set the user groups (learners, course authors and administrators), the core learning loop and success metrics such as course completion. Our guide explains what a discovery phase settles before screens.

items.title: User research (5–15 days)
items.body: Researchers interview 5–8 learners per user group, and course authors, to find where onboarding, lessons and progress tracking lose them. These learner interviews shape every later flow.

items.title: Information architecture and flows (5–10 days)
items.body: The team maps the course structure (courses, course modules and lessons), the learner onboarding flow and the author's publishing flow before any screen is drawn.

items.title: Prototype and validation (10–20 days)
items.body: Five learners per round complete tasks in a clickable Figma prototype on Maze, and each round ends with a usability score, so prototype rounds catch friction before engineering starts.

items.title: UI design and handoff (15–25 days)
items.body: Designers finish every screen state and hand annotated Figma files, design tokens and component specs to your engineers, at WCAG 2.2 level AA. After the developer handoff, the designers stay with your engineers through launch.

sections.h2: Edtech UI/UX design vs instructional design
sections.answer: Edtech UX design decides how learners find, take and track courses on a learning platform; instructional design decides what each online course teaches and in what order. An edtech UI UX design agency tests prototypes with learners before engineering starts, while instructional designers shape the lessons. The table compares both disciplines.

sections.h2: How much do edtech UI/UX design services cost?
sections.answer: Edtech UI/UX design services cost $60,000–$180,000 over 8–16 weeks for a full learning platform, or $25,000–$60,000 over 4–8 weeks for a design sprint.
sections.body: A full edtech engagement uses 3–6 designers; a design sprint uses 2–4, and edtech design services for one surface, for example the course player, run as a sprint. Price follows 4 factors: target platforms (web app, iOS, Android and website), user groups, core user flows such as onboarding, and validation rounds. A UX audit of a live learning platform costs $5,000–$15,000 over 2–3 weeks through our UX audit services.

sections.h2: Which accessibility and privacy standards shape edtech UI/UX design services?
sections.answer: Five accessibility and privacy standards shape edtech UX design for learning platforms, and each one changes what learners see on screen. We design to these standards; legal compliance and certification stay with the product owner.
items: WCAG 2.2 level AA: this accessibility level asks for keyboard access, visible focus and 4.5:1 contrast for normal-size text, so the learner dashboard and course player work without a mouse.

ADA Title II of the Americans with Disabilities Act: the Department of Justice rule requires state and local governments, including public schools and universities, to make web content and mobile apps meet WCAG 2.1 level AA, so platforms sold to them are bought against WCAG.

Section 508: federal agencies must buy accessible information and communication technology, and the Revised 508 Standards incorporate WCAG 2.0 level AA, so learning platforms sold to federal agencies need the same accessible patterns.

Children's Online Privacy Protection Act (COPPA): operators of services directed to children under 13 must get verifiable parental consent before collecting personal information, so sign-up adds a parent consent step and collects only what lessons need.

Family Educational Rights and Privacy Act (FERPA): it protects student education records at schools that receive US Department of Education funds, so role-based views show teachers and administrators only the records they need.

sections.h2: FAQs about edtech UI/UX design services
sections.answer: Before a learning platform team hires an edtech UX design partner, five questions settle the fit: past LMS work, who writes the code, live redesigns, children's products and the website.

faqs.q: Have you designed a learning management system (LMS)?
faqs.a: Yes. For Elia Wellness, a wellness LMS for adults 50+, we took the learning platform from idea to product across web app, mobile app and website. It is our one published edtech project, and the platform reports 40% growth in user registrations.

faqs.q: Do you build the platform or integrate Sharable Content Object Reference Model (SCORM) content?
faqs.a: No. Our designers deliver annotated Figma files, design tokens and component specs, and your engineers write the code. Your team also handles e-learning content standards such as SCORM and integrations with other systems.

faqs.q: Can you redesign a learning platform that is already live?
faqs.a: Yes. Start with a UX audit of the live learning platform, $5,000–$15,000 over 2–3 weeks, that reviews onboarding, the course player and the course builder against usability heuristics and analytics, with a WCAG 2.2 level AA check. Its prioritized fix roadmap then scopes a design sprint.

faqs.q: Can you design an edtech product for children under 13?
faqs.a: Yes. E-learning platform UX design for children follows the same 5 steps, and learner onboarding adds a COPPA parental consent step, with sign-up asking only for the data lessons need. Our published edtech work so far is Elia, which serves older adults, so we do not claim children's products as past work.

faqs.q: Do you design the edtech website as well as the platform?
faqs.a: Yes. Edtech website design for the marketing site that leads learners into the platform runs through our UI UX web design practice. Elia's scope covered its website as well as the web app and mobile app.
